name: Washte Pawne
summary: Across the southern Barrens, Washte Pawne's quill leaves a sting that hunters carry to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo. Its pain makes the hunt a trial of regret for the tauren.

sections.title: The Spirit Biter
sections.body: Thunderhawks are elusive creatures of the Barrens, and wandering nomadic tribes treat them with reverence. Washte Pawne means “Spirit Biter” in Taurahe and holds a special place among them. Its death is no ordinary hunt: shamans whisper that striking down a thunderhawk can bring omens of triumph or misfortune.

sections.title: A Lesson in Regret
sections.body: After Washte Pawne falls, its feather burns with a pain that lingers on the skin. Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo explains that the ache is not poison, but regret. Taking a magnificent life bears a burden. The hunter must face that sorrow and turn it into lasting wisdom.

faq.answer: In Taurahe, the language spoken by the tauren, Washte Pawne means “Spirit Biter.” It is the name of a rare thunderhawk that soars over the southern Barrens.

faq.q: Why does Washte Pawne's feather cause pain?
faq.answer: Jorn Skyseer says the feather’s sting is the sharp pain of regret. It reflects the spiritual cost of ending the life of a magnificent creature.

faq.q: Who do I bring Washte Pawne's Feather to?
faq.answer: Bring the feather to Jorn Skyseer, a tauren elder at Camp Taurajo in the southern Barrens.

faq.q: What omen does slaying a thunderhawk bring?
faq.answer: Tauren tradition says a thunderhawk’s death can herald great fortune or immense doom. Jorn says Washte Pawne’s fall brings neither fate on its own; the hunter must make wisdom from remorse.
Washte Pawne roams the skies of the southern Barrens, often circling the savannah near Camp Taurajo.

faq.q: What does Jorn Skyseer think of you after slaying it?
faq.answer: Jorn does not condemn you. He sees that enduring the quill’s pain means you have mastered regret, turning spiritual grief into strength and understanding.

angles.text: For the Shu'halo, taking Spirit Biter's life is a sacred lesson in respecting nature's balance. It teaches you to turn regret into inner wisdom.
Facing Washte Pawne tests your motives as a hunter. Taking a beast's life carries weight beyond a trophy.
The lingering sting of the thunderhawk's feather reveals the wild's spiritual force, a resonance you can recognize as a shaman who studies elemental harmonies.
At Camp Taurajo, you find a spiritual and hunting crossroads for the Horde, where young warriors face tests of conscience and martial skill.
